questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

This question probes policy-as-code skills, Istio security posture, and CI/CD integration. It tests ability to craft minimal, verifiable manifests and to reason about runtime vs CI checks.

## Key Concepts

- Istio PeerAuthentication mtls: STRICT
- Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate and Constraint
- Kyverno policy or alternative
- CI validation: lint, dry-run apply, policy testing
- Runtime enforcement: Istio sidecars enforce mTLS

## Code Example

```yaml
# Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate sample
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8smtlstrict
spec:
  crd:
    Spec:
      groups: ["constraints.gatekeeper.sh"]
      names:
        kind: K8sMTLSStrict
        plural: k8smTLSStricts
  targets:
    - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
      rego: |
        package k8smtlstrict
        violation["mtls_missing"] {
          input.review.kind.kind == "Namespace"
          not input.review.object.metadata.annotations["istio-injection"]
        }
```

```yaml
# Constraint (example)
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: K8sMTLSStrict
metadata:
  name: mtls-strict
spec:
  match:
    requiredImages: []
```

```yaml
# Passing manifest: PeerAuthentication with mtls: STRICT
apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: PeerAuthentication
metadata:
  name: default
  namespace: default
spec:
  mtls:
    mode: STRICT
```

```yaml
# Failing manifest: missing PeerAuthentication
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: sample
  namespace: test
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: sample
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: sample
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: example/app:latest
```

- How would you enable gradual rollout for mTLS enforcement?
- What exceptions would you permit and how would you audit them?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Immutability of container images is a core security practice. This checks a tangible gating mechanism candidates can implement in a simple CI step.

## Key Concepts

- YAML manifest parsing
- Image digest pinning (immutable refs)
- Lightweight CI scripts in GitHub Actions
- Local verification parity with CI

## Code Example

```yaml
# .github/workflows/pin-digest.yml
name: Pin Image Digests
on:
  push:
    paths:
      - '**/*.yaml'
      - '**/*.yml'
jobs:
  digest_check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Install jq and yq
        run: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y jq wget
      - name: Install yq
        run: wget -qO- https://github.com/mikefarah/yq/releases/download/v4.25.1/yq_linux_amd64 -O /usr/bin/yq && chmod +x /usr/bin/yq
      - name: Validate image digests
        run: |
          DIGESTED=$(yq -r '.. | .image? // empty' **/*.yaml **/*.yml | grep -v '^$' )
          if echo "$DIGESTED" | grep -vq '@sha256:'; then
            echo "Found image refs without digest:";
            echo "$DIGESTED"; exit 1;
          fi
          echo "All images pinned to digests."
```


```yaml
metadata:

spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: myreg/app@sha256:deadbeef...
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to translate security requirements into policy-as-code, enforce across workload types, and validate in CI. It also probes tool choice (Kyverno vs OPA Gatekeeper), namespace scoping, and test design.

## Key Concepts
- Runtime security posture with securityContext fields
- Policy engines: Kyverno, OPA Gatekeeper
- Resource types: Deployments, StatefulSets, DaemonSets
- Local and CI validation strategies

## Code Example
```yaml
# Kyverno cluster policy example
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: enforce-runtime-hardening
spec:
  rules:
  - name: require-secure-pod
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ['Deployment','StatefulSet','DaemonSet']
    validate:
      message: 'Containers must be non-root, readOnlyRootFilesystem, and drop ALL capabilities'
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              containers:
              - name: '*'
                securityContext:
                  runAsNonRoot: true
                  runAsUser: 1000
                  readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
                  allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
                  capabilities:
                    drop: ['ALL']
```

```yaml
# Failing manifest example (violates rules)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: fail-noncompliant
spec:
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: fail
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: example/app:latest
        securityContext:
          runAsUser: 0
          privileged: true
          capabilities:
            add: ['NET_ADMIN']
      volumes:
      - name: data
        hostPath:
          path: /data
```

```yaml
# Passing manifest example
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: compliant
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: example/app:1.2.3
        securityContext:
          runAsNonRoot: true
          runAsUser: 1000
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
          capabilities:
            drop: ['ALL']
```

- Verification steps: locally run kyverno test, simulate with kubectl apply and audit via kyverno CLI; CI gate runs kyverno/opa checks on PR.

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you handle exceptions per-namespace or per-tenant?
- How would you measure false positives in CI across multiple clusters?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Question Is Asked

This question evaluates the ability to design scalable, auditable tenant-isolated admission controls that span both manifest validation and runtime enforcement. It also tests knowledge of secret management integration and canary-driven SLO validation patterns.

## Key Concepts

- **Kyverno & OPA Gatekeeper**: Kubernetes admission control frameworks for policy-as-code
- **Namespace RBAC and tenant isolation**: Role-based access control scoped to per-tenant namespaces
- **SecretStore/secretRef**: External secrets management and secure secret injection
- **PodSecurity Standards**: Built-in Kubernetes pod security policies
- **readOnlyRootFilesystem & resource requests/limits**: Container hardening and resource governance
- **Image digests and canary validation**: Supply chain security and progressive delivery validation
- **Kubernetes Audit API**: Compliance logging and incident replay

## Code Example

```yaml
# Kyverno ClusterPolicy: Enforce SecretStore source
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: secrets-from-external-store
spec:
  validationFailureAction: Enforce
  rules:
    - name: deny-direct-secret-refs
      match:
        resources:
          kinds:
            - Pod
      preconditions:
        - selector:
            matchLabels:
              tenant: restricted
      validate:
        message: "Secrets must be sourced from SecretStore, not direct secretRef."
        pattern:
          spec:
            =(containers):
              - =(env):
                  - =(valueFrom):
                      X(secretRef): "*"  # Deny direct secretRef
                      secretStoreRef: "?*"  # Require SecretStore

# OPA Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate: Deny privileged containers
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: K8sPSPPrivilegedContainer
metadata:
  name: no-privileged-containers
spec:
  match:
    excludedNamespaces: [kube-system]
    kinds:
      - apiGroups: [""]
        kinds: [Pod]

# Kyverno Policy: Enforce image digests
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-image-digests
spec:
  validationFailureAction: Enforce
  rules:
    - name: validate-image-digest
      match:
        resources:
          kinds: [Pod]
      validate:
        message: "Images must use digests, not tags."
        pattern:
          spec:
            containers:
              - image: "!*:*"  # Deny tags, require @sha256:
```

## Sample Manifests

**Failing Pod (privileged container)**:
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: privileged-pod
  namespace: tenant-a
  labels:
    tenant: restricted
spec:
  containers:
    - name: app
      image: nginx@sha256:abc123...
      securityContext:
        privileged: true  # BLOCKED by PSP/Gatekeeper
```

**Passing Pod (compliant)**:
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: compliant-pod
  namespace: tenant-a
  labels:
    tenant: restricted
spec:
  securityContext:
    runAsNonRoot: true
    seccompProfile:
      type: RuntimeDefault
  containers:
    - name: app
      image: nginx@sha256:abc123
      securityContext:
        readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
      resources:
        requests:
          memory: "64Mi"
          cpu: "250m"
        limits:
          memory: "128Mi"
          cpu: "500m"
```

## CI/Local Verification Steps

1. **Install tools**: `kubectl apply -f policy.yaml && kubectl get ClusterPolicy`
2. **Dry-run test**: `kyverno apply policy.yaml --resource manifest.yaml --dry-run`
3. **OPA test**: `conftest verify policy.rego`
4. **CI integration**: Use `kyverno/kyverno-action` in GitHub Actions
5. **Audit replay**: Query `kubectl get events --field-selector reason=PolicyViolation`

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design scalable, enforceable policy gates across clouds with image provenance and hardening.

## Key Concepts
- Image provenance (Sigstore Cosign)
- SecurityContext: RunAsNonRoot, readOnlyRootFilesystem, capabilities.drop ALL
- RBAC: namespace scoping and least privilege
- Policy engines: Kyverno/OPA Gatekeeper
- CI verification: cosign verify, dry-run manifests, local validation

## Code Example
```javascript
name: CI Gate
on:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ main ]
jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: sigstore/cosign-installer@v1
      - name: Verify image signatures
        run: cosign verify --key cosign.pub ${{ env.IMAGE }}
      - name: Validate manifests (dry-run)
        run: kubectl apply --dry-run=server -f k8s/
```

```javascript
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-secure-containers
spec:
  validationFailureAction: enforce
  rules:
  - name: require-security-context
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Deployment","StatefulSet"]
    validate:
      message: "containers must set RunAsNonRoot, readOnlyRootFilesystem, and drop ALL capabilities"
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              containers:
              - securityContext:
                  runAsNonRoot: true
                  readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
                  capabilities:
                    drop:
                    - ALL
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test policy exceptions for service accounts used by CI workflows?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests designing end-to-end security controls across CI and runtime in a multi-cloud Kubernetes environment, combining image signing, registry governance, and host attestation. 

## Key Concepts
- Sigstore/cosign image signing and Rekor attestations
- OPA/Gatekeeper policy constraints for manifests
- Digest pinning and registry allowlists
- TPM/attestation-based runtime scheduling
- End-to-end CI validation and production-time checks

## Code Example
```javascript
// Minimal Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate for image signature
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: K8sImageSig
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sImageSig
        listKind: K8sImageSigList
        plural: k8simagesigs
        singular: k8simagesig
  targets:
    - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
      rego: |
        package k8simagesig
        violation["image unsigned"] {
          input.review.object.kind == "Pod"
          image := input.review.object.spec.containers[_].image
          not image.endswith("@sha256:")
        }
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test revocation of a signed image in CI and runtime?
- How would you handle edge cases like multi- tenant imaging workflows or private registries?
